CHN.note: World's #1 grape producer (~13.5 Mt table grapes 2024, USDA Fresh Apples/Grapes/Pears MY2024). Also #1 producer of pears and a top peach/plum grower, so it dominates this 0806+0808+0809 basket. Grape exports ~480 kt (USDA 2024) to Asian markets (Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand); net importer of the basket once large pear/grape inbound is counted. CAVEAT: basket combines table grapes (0806, dominant), pears (0808) and stone fruit (0809: peaches/nectarines, plums, apricots, cherries).

ITA.note: EU's largest table-grape exporter and a major pear/peach/plum grower; the leading EU node in this 0806+0808+0809 basket. 2024 EU grape crop hit by spring rain in Puglia/Sicily (USDA 2024). Ships grapes, pears and stone fruit to Germany, France, Austria, Switzerland, Poland.

ESP.note: Largest single exporter into the EU basket: Spanish table grapes (Vinalopo, seedless), plus peaches/nectarines (Aragon/Catalonia) and apricots. 2024 (FAOSTAT/USDA): big flows to Germany, France, UK, Italy, Portugal, Poland. Aggregated 0806+0808+0809 export ~0.9 Mt.

USA.note: California table-grape crop rebounded ~31% to ~845 kt in 2024 after 2023 Hurricane Hilary damage (USDA/Capital Press 2024); also a major peach/plum/cherry grower. World's #1 table-grape importer (~760 kt grapes alone, USDA 2024) — adds pears/stone fruit for the basket. Exports to Canada, Mexico, Taiwan, Korea, Japan; imports from Chile, Peru, Mexico (97% of US grape imports).

CHL.note: Southern-Hemisphere counter-seasonal powerhouse: table grapes ~565-570 kt exports (USDA MY2024/25, prod ~723 kt) PLUS large plum, cherry, peach/nectarine and pear exports, which lift the combined 0806+0808+0809 export to ~1.2 Mt. Cherries boomed to China; grapes to the US/China/Hong Kong. Note: basket aggregation, grape-only is the ~0.57 Mt subset.

PER.note: World's #1 table-grape exporter by volume in recent seasons (~595-600 kt grape exports, USDA 2024), Ica/Piura desert production extending the Northern-Hemisphere window. Adds some stone fruit for the basket. Ships to USA, Netherlands, China, Mexico, Hong Kong, UK.

ZAF.note: Major Southern-Hemisphere exporter: table grapes ~310 kt exports (USDA 2024, prod ~342 kt) plus pears, plums, peaches/nectarines and apricots from the Western Cape. Combined 0806+0808+0809 export ~0.5 Mt to the EU (Netherlands, UK), Gulf, Canada.

TUR.note: Huge grape producer (~4.2 Mt, much for raisins/wine; #2 table-grape consumer ~3.0 Mt) and a large apricot/cherry/peach grower (world's #1 apricot producer). Fresh 0806+0808+0809 exports ~0.3 Mt to Russia, Ukraine, EU (Austria, Romania) and the Gulf, 2024 (FAOSTAT).

IND.note: #3 table-grape consumer (~2.8 Mt) and a fast-growing grape exporter from Maharashtra (Nashik) targeting the EU early-season window. 2024 (FAOSTAT): India->Netherlands ~94 kt, India->UK ~16 kt of grapes. Minor pear/stone-fruit role in the basket.

NLD.note: Europe's #1 fruit entrepot (Rotterdam): negligible own production but Europe's leading importer/re-exporter of grapes, pears and stone fruit. Imports from South Africa, Peru, Chile, India, Egypt, Namibia, Spain; re-exports across Germany, Poland, Belgium, France, UK, Scandinavia. 2024 (FAOSTAT).

DEU.note: Largest EU consumer-importer of the basket: imports table grapes, pears and stone fruit from Spain, Netherlands, Italy, Greece, Belgium, Turkey; re-exports some to Poland, Austria, Czechia. 2024 (FAOSTAT). Negligible domestic table-grape production (wine grapes excluded here).

GBR.note: Pure net importer (negligible production): year-round table grapes from South Africa, Spain, Peru, Chile, Egypt, India, Namibia plus pears/stone fruit. UK is ~15% of EU-area grape imports. 2024 (FAOSTAT).

FRA.note: France grows peaches/nectarines, apricots, plums and some table grapes (Muscat) but is a net importer of the basket, sourcing Spanish grapes/stone fruit, Italian and Dutch re-exports. 2024 (FAOSTAT). France->key intra-EU flows plus large Spanish/Italian inbound.

MEX.note: Sonora table grapes fill the May-July US window (~exports to USA ~165 kt, 2024 FAOSTAT) while importing US/Chilean/Peruvian grapes off-season; also a peach/plum trade partner. Net exporter of the basket in 2024 (FAOSTAT/USDA).

RUS.note: Large net importer of grapes, pears and stone fruit (Turkey, Central Asia, Egypt, South America) after EU-trade disruption; domestic grape output mostly wine/southern regions. ~0.42 Mt basket imports, 2024 (FAOSTAT mirror; Russia did not fully report HS0806/0808/0809 to Comtrade 2024).

EGY.note: Major early-season table-grape exporter (Nile Delta), hitting the EU/UK window ahead of South Africa and India; also exports some stone fruit. 2024 (FAOSTAT): Egypt->Netherlands ~34 kt, Egypt->UK ~32 kt, Egypt->Saudi Arabia ~25 kt of basket fruit.

rankings.note: Combined 0806+0808+0809 basket (table grapes dominant, plus pears 0808 and stone fruit 0809: peaches/nectarines, plums, apricots, cherries), volumes in kt 2024, blending USDA FAS Fresh Apples/Grapes/Pears MY2024, FAOSTAT TCL importer-reports and ITC/freshfruitportal trade press. companies.name: Subsole
companies.note: One of Chile's largest table-grape and stone-fruit exporters (also citrus, avocado), shipping ~30+ Mn boxes/yr to the US, China, Europe in 2024. Vertically linked grower network across Chile and Peru.
companies.improve: Should publish Orchard-level water-use intensity and labour-standard audits for its Chilean/Peruvian desert grape operations given Atacama/Ica water stress.

companies.name: Unifrutti Group
companies.note: Global grower-marketer of grapes, cherries, stone fruit and citrus across Chile, South Africa, Europe and Asia; majority-owned by ADQ since 2023, revenue ~US$1bn+ (2024). Major counter-seasonal grape/cherry supplier to China and the EU.
companies.improve: Should disclose pesticide-residue and water-stewardship metrics across its multi-origin grape and stone-fruit estates.

companies.name: Sun World International
companies.note: World's leading table-grape genetics/IP licensor (Autumncrisp, Sable Seedless, Adora and other proprietary varieties); licenses growers across 15+ countries and collects royalties on a large share of premium seedless grapes traded in 2024.
companies.improve: Should report how its variety-licensing royalties flow back to smallholder licensees and whether breeding targets lower-water, heat-tolerant cultivars.

companies.name: Capespan
companies.note: Historic South African fruit exporter (grapes, pears, plums, citrus) and a core node moving Western Cape and Orange/Hex River grapes to the EU, UK and Gulf in 2024. Part of the broader FruitOne/AgriGroup structure after restructuring.
companies.improve: Should publish farm-worker wage and housing-condition data for its Western Cape grower base and Orange River water-allocation exposure.

companies.name: Greenyard
companies.note: One of Europe's largest fresh-produce groups (revenue ~EUR 5bn, FY2024), a leading importer/distributor of table grapes, pears and stone fruit into EU retail via its Benelux/German hubs. Key buyer in the Rotterdam/Antwerp entrepot trade.
companies.improve: Should disclose supplier-level traceability and residue-monitoring results for its multi-origin grape and stone-fruit ranges.

companies.name: Dole plc
companies.note: Global fresh-produce major (revenue ~US$8bn, FY2024) with table-grape and deciduous-fruit sourcing across Chile, Peru, South Africa and North America for US and EU retail. Operates its own cold-chain and shipping in 2024.
companies.improve: Should report water-use and agrochemical metrics for its South American grape estates and the carbon intensity of its reefer logistics.

global.note: Combined fresh table grapes (0806) + pears (0808) + stone fruit (0809: peaches/nectarines, plums, apricots, cherries) world totals, kt, blending USDA FAS Fresh Apples/Grapes/Pears MY2024 (world table grapes ~27-28 Mt, China ~13.5 Mt) with FAOSTAT pear/stone-fruit output. 2024 fresh-grape global exports alone rose ~12% to ~4.8 Mt (IndexBox/ITC); the wider basket including pears and stone fruit is ~10 Mt traded. Excludes wine/raisin grapes.

forecast.method: OECD-FAO/USDA envelope; 2030=2024×(1+rate)^6. Table-grape demand grows ~2-3%/yr on premium-seedless and Asian retail expansion; Peru/Chile/South Africa/China lead supply growth, EU pear/stone-fruit output flat to declining on aging orchards and climate stress (spring frost, hail). Trade outpaces production as Northern markets pull more counter-seasonal fruit.
